characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Fischerscope H100 microhardness tester (maximum load 1 N); HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 300 °C/3 d anneal gives a hardness equal to that of the as-grown monocrystal, ≈2000 N/mm²; overall hardness varies only by about 10% at most with heat treatment, i.e. short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; values averaged over more than 40 measurements; (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal annealed at 300 °C/3 d
characterization_methods.purpose: to determine the effect of prior heat treatment (state of atomic order) on the hardness/mechanical behaviour of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM-based EDX for qualitative precipitate/inclusion analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: The monocrystals contain rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm.
characterization_methods.purpose: qualitative identification of inclusions present in the monocrystals

processing_steps.duration: about 12 h (crystal growth with subsequent cooling)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Monocrystals with up to 10 cm length grown by the Bridgman method; crystal growth with subsequent cooling occurred within a time period of about 12 h. Monocrystals were etched by ammonium persulfate and oriented using a laser light-figure method. This is the fabrication history of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal specimen.

300 °C/3 day anneal of the (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal; one of a series of 300 °C anneals of different durations; produces an intermediate degree of order. Specimens were cut by electrostatic discharge machining and mechanically polished; heat treatments up to 300 °C were done in high-purity argon.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Microhardness tester Fischerscope H100 (maximum load 1 N); universal hardness HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]; reported HU values are averages of more than 40 measurements; the specimen was given the 300 °C/3 day anneal before testing

inclusions: rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm, identified by EDX

phases_present.phase_name: Fe–Al solid solution with short-range order (K-state)

phases_present.morphology: rare globular inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm

structures.overall_structure: Single crystal (monocrystal) of Fe-16%Al; the specimens used for the hardness study were (111)-oriented. No grain boundaries (monocrystalline); rare globular AlN inclusions present.

unmapped_findings: The various heat treatments of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal specimens result in different states of short-range order: maximum ordering after the 250 °C/14 day anneal, minimum ordering after quenching from 1100 or 600 °C, and intermediate degrees of order for the other treatments in Fig. 1 — hence the 300 °C/3 day anneal corresponds to an intermediate degree of order (b0050).
The hardness of the 300 °C/3 d-annealed Fe-16%Al monocrystal equals that of the as-grown monocrystal; it is concluded that short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness (b0050).
Only heat treatments at temperatures above 600 °C affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys significantly (b0051, b0067).

Excess vacancies (introduced by quenching, not by the 300 °C anneal itself) heal out only slowly; the annealing at 300 °C of the Fe-Al alloys even for 14 days may not have been sufficient for the complete elimination of the excess vacancies (b0055).
